temperature.name: sampling temperature
temperature.definition: A positive divisor applied to logits before softmax to control distribution sharpness.
temperature.explanation: Temperature below one magnifies logit differences and makes high-score tokens more likely. Temperature above one flattens the distribution and increases diversity. At temperature one, probabilities are unchanged. Zero is undefined for this sampling rule; greedy decoding should be implemented explicitly as argmax. Temperature changes generation behavior without retraining and does not repair a weak model. Byte-level sampling may emit invalid UTF-8, so preserve bytes and treat lossy conversion as display only.

resource-budget.name: resource budget
resource-budget.definition: An explicit accounting of parameters, persistent state, activations, time, and hardware for a run.
resource-budget.explanation: Parameter count gives a lower bound on storage, not peak training memory. f32 weights require four bytes each; Adam first and second moments add eight more persistent bytes per parameter. Gradients, activations, attention probabilities, allocator overhead, GPU staging, and checkpoint copies add further memory. Throughput must be measured with a release build and reported with shapes, precision, hardware, and flags. Tiny-model measurements should not be extrapolated as claims about a much larger configuration.
